answer.summary: The 2x discrepancy is a fan-out artifact, not a data-quality mystery in the amount itself. The evidence shows order grain is declared as one row per order (order_grain = "one_per_order"), yet items_per_order = 2, so each order row replicates twice when joined to its line items: the order-level total of 10000 cents appears once (credible at order grain), while the joined result of 20000 cents is simply 10000 x 2 identical copies. The credible figure for order total is the order-grain 10000; the 20000 must never be reported as revenue because it double-counts a non-additive order-level measure. Troubleshooting path: (1) confirm the intended output grain (order vs. item) and the declared grain of each source; (2) verify that joined_orders_cents / orders_cents equals items_per_order exactly, which it does (2.0), a signature of a pure 1:N fan-out rather than a real amount change; (3) de-duplicate to one row per order before summing order-level amounts, or push all sums to the item grain using item-level prices that reconcile to the order total; (4) reconcile item subtotals against the order total as a control check.
limitations: No item-level amount/price column is present, so the item subtotals cannot be verified to sum to the order total of 10000 cents; only the aggregate duplication ratio is observable.

Order grain is given only as a descriptive string (one row per order) with no key or unique event identifier, so the presence of exactly 2 item rows per order is inferred from items_per_order rather than proven by a join key.
No timestamps, session or exposure data are supplied, so no conversion, refund or retention metric can be evaluated here.
The evidence does not indicate whether other order-level fields (discounts, shipping, tax) would also be double-counted under the same join, so the full scope of affected measures remains unchecked.
